title: Google's Pixel 11 Pro Fold Unveils a Faster Future for Charging
summary: The Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold promises a significantly upgraded charging experience, leveraging both rapid wired and enhanced wireless technologies. Users can expect 50% battery in 30 minutes via wired charging and a speed boost from the new 25W Qi2 wireless standard, all in a lighter form factor.
content:
Google's latest entry into the competitive foldable market, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, isn't just about its innovative design or enhanced processing power. Underneath its sleek, re-engineered chassis lies a significant upgrade to its power delivery system, promising users less time tethered to an outlet and more time experiencing their device.

For those moments when every second counts, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold truly shines. Google has engineered the device to reach a 50% charge in a mere 30 minutes when paired with a 30W or higher Power Delivery Programmable Power Supply (PPS) charger. This rapid replenishment ensures that even a quick coffee break can give your foldable enough juice to power through hours of use, making frantic scrambles for an outlet a thing of the past.

Beyond the wired prowess, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold also steps up its wireless game. Embracing the newer Qi2 standard, the device now supports a robust 25W wireless charging. This isn't just about raw speed, however; Qi2 brings with it improved efficiency and better thermal management, translating into a faster, safer, and more consistent wireless charging experience compared to previous iterations. It’s a meaningful leap forward for untethered power delivery.

Crucially, this improved efficiency and charging speed come without compromise on endurance. Despite arriving in a lighter, more portable package, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold retains the exact same impressive battery life claim as its predecessor, the Pixel 10 Pro Fold. This commitment to maintaining all-day power, coupled with accelerated charging capabilities, positions the 11 Pro Fold as a device optimized for the modern, on-the-go user.

Google appears to be striking a thoughtful balance with the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, offering not just a lighter device, but one that’s far more convenient to keep powered up. It’s a testament to the continued evolution of mobile technology, where user experience and practical performance are paramount.
keyTakeaways: The Pixel 11 Pro Fold achieves 50% battery charge in just 30 minutes using a 30W or higher PPS wired charger.
It features significantly faster 25W wireless charging thanks to the adoption of the new Qi2 standard.
Despite being a lighter device, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold maintains the same strong battery life claim as its predecessor.
author: roydon.cerejo@gmail.com (Roydon Cerejo) , Roydon Cerejo

title: Truth Social's $100,000 'Early Access' Feed Sparks Insider Trading Accusations
summary: Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG) has launched a controversial premium subscription service, offering Wall Street firms early access to Truth Social posts for $100,000 monthly. This move has ignited a fierce debate over potential insider trading and the monetization of political influence through digital platforms.
content:
Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG) has dropped a bombshell into the tech and finance worlds, unveiling a premium data product that allows select Wall Street firms early access to Truth Social posts for a staggering $100,000 per month. This high-priced subscription has immediately ignited a firestorm of ethical questions, with critics swiftly labeling it as a blatant attempt to monetize political influence and even as a form of "insider trading by definition."

The proposition is stark: pay six figures, get ahead. In an era where a single tweet or social media pronouncement from a prominent figure can send markets soaring or plummeting, the allure of pre-publication access is undeniable for financial institutions. TMTG positions this as a "premium data product," but the implication is clear — early insights into the thought processes and announcements of Donald Trump and other key figures on the platform could offer a significant, potentially market-moving, advantage.

The ethical quagmire here is profound. Experts are already scrutinizing whether providing privileged access to information that could influence market sentiment, based on a political figure's platform, crosses legal boundaries into insider trading. This isn't merely about exclusive content; it's about the potential for economic gain derived from information that isn't yet publicly available. The specter of "monetizing the presidency," even post-presidency, looms large, raising concerns about fairness and transparency in both financial markets and political discourse.

Despite the immediate backlash, the appetite for such a service appears robust. Reports indicate at least five prominent Wall Street firms have already signed on, underscoring the perceived value of this exclusive feed. This move by TMTG highlights the evolving, often controversial, intersection of social media platforms, political power, and high finance, challenging established norms and pushing the boundaries of what constitutes fair play in information access. The coming months will undoubtedly see continued debate and potentially regulatory scrutiny as this audacious business model unfolds.
keyTakeaways: Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG) has launched a $100,000 monthly subscription service for Wall Street firms.
The service offers early, premium access to Truth Social posts, implying a potential market advantage.
Critics are fiercely debating the ethics, with many labeling it as a form of insider trading and an unacceptable monetization of political influence.
author: Fortune

title: Google Snags AWS Public Sector Chief in Major Cloud War Play
summary: Dave Levy, the Vice President of AWS Worldwide Public Sector, has departed Amazon Web Services to join its competitor Google. This high-profile executive move is a significant development in the fiercely competitive cloud computing market, particularly impacting the public sector.
content:
The battle for cloud dominance just got a significant new twist. Dave Levy, the highly respected Vice President of AWS Worldwide Public Sector, has officially departed the industry behemoth, making a high-profile jump to one of its fiercest rivals: Google. His last day at Amazon Web Services was Friday, July 31, marking the end of a pivotal tenure that began in 2017.

Levy’s move sends ripples across the tech landscape, signaling yet another escalation in the fiercely competitive cloud wars. During his time at AWS, Levy was instrumental in driving the company's formidable presence in government, education, and non-profit sectors globally. This portfolio includes critical contracts and strategic partnerships with entities like the Department of Defense and numerous public service organizations, making it a cornerstone of AWS’s expansive market leadership. His expertise and network in this sensitive and lucrative arena are second to none.

For Google Cloud, this is a clear strategic coup. While Google has made significant strides, it has consistently trailed AWS and Microsoft Azure in market share, especially within the complex public sector space. Bringing Levy on board is a powerful statement of intent, suggesting a renewed, aggressive push to capture a larger slice of these high-value government and educational workloads. His intimate knowledge of AWS’s strategy and operational mechanics in this domain could prove invaluable for Google.

This executive shuffle underscores the intense talent acquisition skirmishes defining today’s cloud market. Top-tier leadership with deep industry expertise is a scarce commodity, and companies are willing to go to great lengths to poach seasoned veterans who can tilt the competitive scales. Levy’s departure from AWS, and his immediate transition to a direct competitor, is more than just a personnel change; it’s a strategic maneuver that could redefine portions of the public sector cloud battleground for years to come.
keyTakeaways: Dave Levy, a key AWS executive, has left for Google, a primary competitor.
His move intensifies the fierce competition between AWS and Google Cloud, especially in the lucrative public sector.
This signals a new phase in the ongoing talent wars within the rapidly expanding cloud computing industry.
author: Frank Konkel
